summary: The Record a termination picker listed candidates still in onboarding (no employee ID). It now loads a dedicated list of active employees only (ACTIVE, with an employee ID, not past an approved last working day, not already terminated), and the server refuses a termination of anyone who is not an active employee.
testSteps: 1. Log in as Company Super Admin. 2. Separation > Terminations > Record a termination. 3. Type the name of a candidate who is still in onboarding (e.g. status 'Filling details'). Expected: the candidate does not appear; only active employees with an employee ID are listed.
negativeTests: 1. (API) POST /api/v2/admin/employees/<candidate id>/terminate. Expected 409: 'Only active employees can be terminated. This person is still a candidate in onboarding (or has already left) — manage them from Onboarding instead.'
automated: scripts/v2/test-workflow-exit.js — 'candidate not offered', 'v2: terminating a candidate refused', 'v1 contract unchanged (still accepted)'
v1Impact: None (v2 only) — the v1 terminate endpoint keeps its old checks; the new picker endpoint is v2-only.

summary: The NFA queue printed raw codes (PENDING, PAYMENT RELEASED, ADVANCE SELF). It now uses readable labels everywhere: filters, rows, detail and chain. An HR override approved or queried with no confirmation and was recorded under the stage approver's name. Now every Approve / Query / Reject asks for confirmation. If you are not the stage approver, the dialog says it is an HR override, names the stage and its approver, and lists any later stages with no approver that will then be skipped. The action is recorded under the acting HR user (stage shows "Actioned by <you> (HR override)", and the trail is marked as an override). When an NFA is on query, the admin now sees "Waiting for <employee> to reply" and can still close it with "Reject without waiting". The employee replies to the query with text and can attach the requested bill (PDF/image).
testSteps: 1. Log in as HR. Open NFA & Finance > NFA Queue. Expected: the Status and Payment type filters read "Payment released", "Advance (self)", "Reimbursement (self)", "PPS candidate"; no raw codes. 2. Open a pending NFA whose current stage belongs to someone else, type a remark and click Approve. Expected: a confirmation says "This is an HR override of the Reporting Manager stage (approver: …) and will be recorded under your name" and lists later stages that will be skipped. Confirm. Expected: the chain row shows "Actioned by <HR name> (HR override)" while the approver name stays the stage approver. 3. On another pending NFA click Raise query with remark "Attach bill". 4. Log in as the Employee > NFA > My NFAs > open that NFA. Type a reply, attach a PDF bill and click Resubmit. Expected: the NFA returns to Pending and the PDF is listed under Attachments as "Query reply: …". 5. As HR, query it again and open it. Expected: "Waiting for … to reply" and a "Reject without waiting" button.
negativeTests: 1. Click Raise query or Reject with an empty remark. Expected: "Remarks are required to reject or raise a query." 2. As the Employee, click Resubmit with an empty reply. Expected: "Your reply is required". 3. Click Cancel on the override confirmation. Expected: nothing is recorded.
automated: scripts/v2/test-workflow-nfa.js — 'HR query is recorded under the HR user, not the stage approver', 'trail marks the override', 'reply is required (v2)', 'employee resubmits with the bill', 'HR can close an NFA that sits on query'
v1Impact: Applies to v1 too — acting-user recording and the extra columns are additive (new response keys actedBy/override only). On an override the stage keeps its approver instead of being overwritten with the HR's employee id, which only corrects whose name is shown. Rejecting a queried NFA as staff is a new capability; it does not change any existing v1 call. Requiring a reply text is v2 only.

Open Expense Hierarchy. Expected: each row has Deactivate and Delete buttons, and Delete asks "Delete \"…\"?".

Add a header with the same name, different case, under the same category. Expected: refused as a duplicate.

summary: The Approvers stage list only had matrix stages, so Reporting Manager, Functional Head/Manager, Office Admin and Human Resource could never be assigned. It also allowed one person on every stage, and saving the same approver twice was silently ignored. Now the list covers every stage of every chain (NFA, settlement, resignation, PMS). Each stage shows which chains use it, whether it is required, and how it is used. For a manager stage, the row applies when the employee has no such manager. The engine now honours these rows. Saving an approver who already holds other stages shows a confirmation listing them. Replacing an existing approver asks first. Saving the identical approver again is refused with "<Name> is already the Finance approver for this scope" (409).
testSteps: 1. Log in as Company Super Admin. Open NFA & Finance > Approvers. Open the Stage dropdown. Expected: Reporting Manager (required), Functional Head, Functional Manager, Office Admin, Human Resource (required), Finance, Business Head, etc. Choosing one shows e.g. "Resignation, Settlement · Normally the employee's own manager…". 2. Choose Finance, pick employee X and click Save. 3. Choose Business Head, pick the same X and click Save. Expected: a confirmation "X already approves: Finance…"; click Save anyway. 4. Choose Reporting Manager, pick a manager and click Save. Then, as an employee with no reporting manager, open Create NFA. Expected: stage 1 of the approval chain shows that manager.
negativeTests: 1. Save Finance = X with the same scope again. Expected: "X is already the Finance approver for this scope." 2. Save with no stage or approver. Expected: "Choose a stage" / "Choose an approver".
automated: scripts/v2/test-workflow-nfa.js — 'stage list covers manager-chain and named stages', 'stages carry readable labels', 'saving the same approver twice → 409 with a message', 'approver who already holds a stage is reported (alsoApproves)', 'a Reporting Manager row on the Approvers page now staffs the stage', 'v1: unchanged (silent replace)'
v1Impact: Mostly v2 only: the 409 duplicate and stage validation are v2. The engine fallback (a manager or named stage with nobody uses the Approvers row for the same stage) applies to both versions. It only takes effect once an admin assigns such a row, which v1 could not offer before. Existing chains are snapshots and are unaffected.

summary: The help text wrongly pointed employees to 'NFA > Vendor Registration'; it now says they register vendors from the employee portal's Vendors menu. Admins can now add a vendor directly (Add vendor), which is approved straight away. A vendor can no longer be approved unless its statutory details are complete and valid (PAN is mandatory; GSTIN, ESIC, PF, MSME and NSIC are optional but must be well-formed). Approve now asks for confirmation. Rejecting a vendor or an agreement requires a reason, which is stored and shown to the employee.
testSteps: 1. Log in as Company Super Admin. Open Vendors & Agreements. Expected: the subtitle says employees register from the employee portal's Vendors menu. 2. Click Add vendor and enter Company 'Sunrise Facility Services', Type 'Private Limited', PAN 'ABCPS1234K', GSTIN '21ABCPS1234K1Z5', plus bank details. Click Add vendor. Expected: the vendor appears under the Approved filter, marked 'Added by admin'. 3. Choose the Pending approval filter and click Approve on a valid pending vendor. Expected: a confirmation appears; after you confirm, the status is Approved and the card shows 'Reviewed by <you> on <date>'. 4. Click Reject on another pending vendor, type 'PAN card missing' and confirm. Expected: Rejected, and 'Reason: PAN card missing' is shown. 5. Log in as that Employee and open Vendors. Expected: the row shows Rejected with the reason.
negativeTests: 1. Approve a pending vendor that has no PAN (one registered from the old mobile app). Expected error: 'Complete the vendor's statutory details before approving — PAN is required'. 2. Click Reject and leave the reason empty. Expected: 'Reason is required', and the dialog stays open. 3. Add vendor with every field empty. Expected: all errors at once, including 'Company name is required', 'Type of company is required' and 'PAN is required'.
automated: scripts/v2/test-workflow-vendor.js: 'C35: vendor with invalid/missing statutory details cannot be approved', 'reject without reason → 400', 'reject with reason stored', 'employee sees the rejection reason', 'admin-added vendor is approved immediately', 'admin add validates every field at once', 'employee cannot use the admin add'
v1Impact: The v1 review endpoint behaves as before: no reason is required and there is no statutory check on approve. A reason sent by an old client is now stored. Admin add is a new v2-only route.

summary: The grade ladder was read-only and global, and a KPI from someone with no reporting manager sat at 'RM pending' forever. Each organisation can now edit its own grade ladder (PMS / KPI > Grade system > Edit grades; codes, labels and 'from %' per grade, validated so there are no gaps or overlaps), or reset to the standard ladder. Final grades use the employee's organisation's ladder. A KPI raised by an employee with no (active) reporting manager is routed to HR: the employee is told so, it appears in HR's 'KPI approvals' tab marked 'no reporting manager — HR approves', and HR can approve or send it back. PMS rating stages that nobody holds now appear in HR's Rating queue so HR can rate them.
testSteps: 1. Log in as Company Super Admin > PMS / KPI > Grade system > Edit grades. 2. Change AT's 'From %' to 95 and its label, Save ladder, confirm. Expected: table shows the new ranges as '95% to below 105%' and the header says 'Your organisation's own grade ladder'. 3. Log in as an employee with no reporting manager (e.g. TH5001) > Performance > Submit KPI for the current month. Expected: a note says the KPI goes to HR; status shows 'Pending with HR'. 4. Log in as HR > PMS / KPI > KPI approvals. Expected: the KPI is listed with 'no reporting manager — HR approves'; Approve (confirm) locks it. 5. Employee submits PMS; HR > Rating queue shows it with 'nobody assigned — HR rates'; rate it; the final grade uses the organisation ladder.
negativeTests: 1. Edit grades with the lowest 'From %' = 10. Expected: 'The lowest grade must start at 0%, or a low score would get no grade.' 2. Two grades with codes 'ab' and 'AB'. Expected: 'Code AB is used twice'. 3. Blank label. Expected: 'Label is required'. 4. Grade 2 starting below grade 1. Expected: 'A higher grade must start at a higher percentage.' 5. Another organisation's admin cannot see or approve this KPI (404). 6. An employee calling the ladder save gets 403.
automated: scripts/v2/test-workflow-pms.js — 'HR saves a custom ladder', 'lowest grade must start at 0%', 'duplicate code (case-insensitive)...', 'another organisation still has the default ladder', 'KPI without an RM is routed to HR with a notice', 'v2: HR sees it in KPI approvals', 'another organisation’s admin cannot approve it (404)', 'v2: HR rating queue shows a stage nobody holds', '104.5% graded on the organisation ladder (A)'
v1Impact: v1 GET /pms/grades keeps its array shape (adds upperPct/rangeLabel; serves the org's ladder if one was configured in v2). Final grading uses the org ladder on both versions — only differs once an org configures one. v1 team-pending / rating queue unchanged (HR extras are v2 only).

summary: Root causes: (a) /meta/nfa-masters scoped by the account's organisation, so an account with no organisation saw every tenant's masters; (b) master ids on an NFA were never checked against the raiser's organisation; (c) one NFA counter for the whole deployment; (d) the chain resolved the requester as his own Finance approver and stalled on an empty mandatory Reporting Manager stage. Now: masters are always the employee's own organisation's (both versions); a foreign master id is refused; numbering is per organisation (the organisation that already owns the plain NFA2026xxxx numbers continues them, every other organisation gets its own series prefixed with its code, e.g. TH-NFA20260001); in v2 nobody is resolved as approver of their own NFA and an NFA cannot be raised while a required stage has no approver — the form shows which stage and tells the employee to ask HR; optional stages with no approver are skipped, as the Approvers page says.
testSteps: 1. Log in as an Employee of the Company Admin organisation (e.g. TH5001) > NFA > Create NFA. Expected: Business Operation / Project / Location / Client dropdowns show only this organisation's entries (no BJP Call Center, True Kind Foundation, cvf, Dmeo). 2. With project, category and zone chosen, check the Approval chain card. Expected: every stage shows an approver or "Skipped (no approver)"; a required stage without one shows "Not assigned — required" and a red note. 3. Once HR has assigned the stages, submit an NFA. Expected: its number is this organisation's own series (e.g. <ORGCODE>-NFA20260001), not the next TRUE HR number.
negativeTests: 1. If the employee is himself the Finance approver for the project, Submit. Expected: "You are the Finance approver for this project, and you cannot approve your own NFA. Ask HR to assign a different Finance on the Approvers page." 2. With no Reporting Manager: "No Reporting Manager approver is set up for you, so this NFA cannot be raised yet. Ask HR to assign one on the Approvers page." 3. Posting another organisation's project id: "Project is not one of your organisation's options".
automated: scripts/v2/test-workflow-nfa.js — 'org 1 employee does not see org 2 projects', 'an account with no organisation sees its employee\'s organisation only (v1 too)', 'another organisation\'s project on an NFA is refused (v2)', '… and on v1 (cross-tenant leak fix)', 'mandatory Finance stage with nobody → NFA cannot be raised', 'self-approval → refused with a clear message', 'org 2 gets its own series starting at 0001'
v1Impact: Applies to v1 too for the leak fixes (masters scoping, foreign master id refused — an ownerless master is still accepted, as before) and numbering (the code string format is unchanged for the legacy-owner organisation; other organisations get a prefixed code, still a string). Self-approval block and the "required stage must be staffed" check are v2 only.

summary: The resignation Approvals card read the approver matrix with no organisation filter, so another company's employee was shown TRUE HR's Business Head and Finance. The preview now resolves every stage exactly as the approval engine does, using only the employee's own organisation (approver matrix, managers and default approvers must all be in the same organisation). The engine's matrix lookup was also tightened to the exact organisation.
testSteps: 1. Log in as an employee of the Company Admin organisation (e.g. TH5001). 2. Resignation > My Resignation, scroll to Approvals. Expected: only approvers set on that organisation's Approvers page (or its own managers) are shown; no TRUE HR employees (TKF…).
negativeTests: 1. In TRUE HR, assign Business Head = TKF5002 on Approvers. 2. Log in as the other organisation's employee and open Resignation. Expected: Business Head shows 'Not assigned — this step will be skipped', never TKF5002.
automated: scripts/v2/test-workflow-exit.js — 'v2: other org's employee sees no TRUE HR approvers', 'v1: other org's employee sees no TRUE HR approvers', 'own org employee sees own Business Head & Finance'

HR > Separation > Resignations. Expected: the row shows 'Shortfall 20 day(s) — recover in F&F'; Export CSV has 'Notice shortfall (days)' = 20.
negativeTests: 1. LWD before resignation date. Expected: 'Last working date cannot be before the resignation date'.

v1Impact: None for v1 requests (shortfall stays 0); new response fields only.

summary: Employees stayed ACTIVE after their approved last working day. A new exit job (runs at start-up and hourly, acting once per exit) marks every employee whose approved resignation or live termination has a last working day before today (India time) as Inactive — removing them from payroll, org chart, pickers and counts — and disables their login. Every list that uses the shared 'active employee' rule also already excludes anyone past an approved LWD.
testSteps: 1. HR approves a resignation with LWD = yesterday (or wait for the LWD to pass). 2. Within an hour after midnight IST: Employees list. Expected: the employee is Inactive; Resignations > Approved shows 'Exited · login closed <date>'.
negativeTests: 1. LWD = today. Expected: the employee is still Active today (access ends after the LWD, not on it).
automated: scripts/v2/test-workflow-exit.js — 'on the last working day itself the employee is still active', 'employee INACTIVE after LWD', 're-run is a no-op', 'HR sees exitedAt'
v1Impact: Applies to v1 too (background job). It only acts after an approved last working day, so it cannot affect an active employee.

summary: Exited employees could still sign in. The exit job disables the login account after the last working day and drops the cached session context, so even an open session stops working on its next request. Login on both web (v2) and app (v1) is refused.
testSteps: 1. After an employee's approved LWD has passed, try to sign in as that employee on the web and the app. Expected: sign-in refused (account disabled).
negativeTests: 1. Before the LWD passes, the resigning employee can still sign in (D2).
automated: scripts/v2/test-workflow-exit.js — 'login DISABLED after LWD', 'sign-in refused', 'sign-in refused on v1 too'
v1Impact: Applies to v1 too — the job only acts after an approved LWD.

summary: Masters used by HR's NFAs and approver rules ("QA Test Project v2", "East Zone") were stamped on another organisation, or on none, so HR's Masters page showed "No entries". A one-time, idempotent data repair (migration 60_workflow_nfa.js) re-attaches a master to the organisation whose NFAs, approver rows or agreements use it. It does this only when exactly one organisation uses it, its current owner does not, and that organisation has no master with the same name. Expense headers and sub-headers follow their category. New masters are always created on the admin's organisation, and the screens now read the employee's organisation (C46), so it cannot recur.

negativeTests: 1. A master used by two organisations is left where it is (shared use cannot be split automatically). The lead's data clean-up handles any such rows.
automated: scripts/v2/test-workflow-nfa.js — 'an ownerless project used by org 1 now belongs to org 1', 'a zone stamped on org 2 but used only by org 1 moves to org 1', 'HR now sees it on the Masters page'
v1Impact: Applies to v1 too — data repair only; it never moves a master that its owner organisation uses.

summary: The approver dropdown listed people whose last working day had passed. The Approvers page now loads approvers from a new list of current employees only (active, with an employee code, not past an approved last working day), and v2 refuses to save anyone else. The approval engine never routes a stage to someone who has left (deactivated, past an approved resignation LWD, or past an active termination's last day); that stage is treated as having no approver. Rows the exit job flags for reassignment are ignored by the engine and shown on the Approvers page with a "Needs reassignment" badge and a warning banner. The flag itself is set by the exit worker (owned by the workflow lead). The exit job (services/exitWorker.js, started from server.js) sets needs_reassignment on every approver row of an employee once their last working day has passed.

notes: Workflow split into sub-areas: routes/v2/workflow.js mounts routes/v2/workflow/{nfa,vendor,pms,exit}.js; scripts/v2/test-workflow.js runs test-workflow-{nfa,vendor,pms,exit}.js each in its own process and sums them (re-runnable on the same DB). New worker services/exitWorker.js started in server.js (hourly + at boot; acts once per exit, only after the LWD in IST). Engine (approvalEngine.js) changes used by resignation/PMS too: exitedSql() export, matrix fallback for manager_chain/named_user stages, needs_reassignment ignored, previewChain/createInstance accept { noSelf }, preview items carry roleLabel/optional/missing, STAGE_LABELS/stageLabel exported, act() records acted_by_user_id/acted_by_name/is_override (columns from 60_workflow_nfa.js) and lets staff REJECT an instance in QUERY. 'Exited' deliberately does not use activeEmployeeSql in the engine (old fixtures have managers without ACTIVE/code); the picker does. NFA numbering: the first organisation to number NFAs (or, on an upgraded DB, the one with most existing NFAs) keeps NFA<yyyy><nnnn>; others get <ORGCODE>-NFA<yyyy><nnnn>; collisions with the old shared counter are skipped.  Tenancy (both versions): vendors and agreements are now scoped on COALESCE(row.organisation_id, employee.organisation_id). Previously they were scoped only through an inner join to the employee, so a vendor added by an admin login with no employee record belonged to no tenant. Agreement project/location/client ids that belong to another organisation are refused on both versions. Decision on 'statutory details before approval': PAN is mandatory (and must be valid); GSTIN is optional because unregistered small vendors are legitimate, but if given it must be valid and match the PAN; all other given identifiers must be valid. The shared form components live in web/app/admin/vendors/vendorForms.jsx and are imported by the ESS page. Grade lookup is floor-based on both versions (wrong-data fix). Per-org ladder falls back to the global pms_grades. Employees with no organisation (legacy rows, as in scripts/test-pms.js) use the global ladder. KPI create/update now accept an optional per-KRA target on both versions (additive). approvalEngine.js untouched.
